title: submission.csv row contract

x-provenance.status: AUTHORED — not supplied by the organiser
why: The problem statement contains no submission schema. Verified by full read of all six pages.
Section 11 names 'submission.csv' and describes it only as 'Predictions in the required format'.

The sole enumeration anywhere is a prose phrase in Section 6 describing submission_template.csv: 'Required output format for probabilities, next state, exception type, anomaly score, top drivers, action, and confidence.' That phrase supplies no identifier-form column names, no order, no dtypes, no ranges, no allowed-value sets, and no row key.
Section 7's field list is introduced as 'Example fields include' and its target sentence as 'should include', so both are explicitly illustrative rather than normative.
derivation: Column set = the 7 target names printed in Section 7, mapped onto the 7 output items printed in Section 6, plus a row key.

Section 7 names the targets as *_flag; Section 6 requires *probabilities*. Probability columns therefore carry a _prob suffix and the flag-name mapping is recorded in x-target-mapping below. This is a naming decision, not a transcription.

exception_type values are derived from Section 6's own description of validation_rules.json ('balance consistency, date validity, delinquency consistency, closed/prepaid status, and document gaps') and of servicer_updates.csv ('source conflict detection, stale record logic, and reconciliation'), so the taxonomy is grounded in the document's wording rather than invented.
next_state values are authored; the document never enumerates a state space. See research.md section 14.
recommended_action values are authored; the document never enumerates an action set.
known_document_inconsistencies: Section 6 prints 'submission_template.csv'; Sections 9 and 11 print 'submission.csv'. This contract targets the deliverable name, submission.csv.
Section 6 prints 'next state' and 'exception type' with spaces; Section 7 prints next_state and exception_type with underscores. This contract uses the Section 7 identifier form.
x-provenance.supersession: If an organiser-supplied submission_template.csv arrives, it supersedes this file. Downstream code reads the contract from this path, so replacing it is a configuration change, not a code change.

x-granularity.basis: spec.md Assumption 4. The document states no row key; the prediction unit is used, which is the reading most consistent with Section 7's per-loan-month field list.
x-granularity.uniqueness: The pair (loan_id, reporting_month) MUST be unique across the file.
x-granularity.sort: Rows MUST be sorted ascending by loan_id then reporting_month. Required for the byte-identity guarantee in FR-071 / SC-002.

x-csv-format.note: No field may contain a comma, quote, or newline, so the file needs no quoting at all. top_drivers uses ';' as its internal separator for this reason.

loan_id.description: Loan Sequence Number. Origination field 20 = performance field 1 in the Release 47 layout.

reporting_month.description: As-of month as YYYYMM, matching the source encoding exactly (performance field 2). Integer rather than a formatted date string so that sort order is total and byte-stable.

next_3m_delinquency_prob.description: P(any month in (m, m+3] has delinquency status >= 1). Calibrated.

next_6m_delinquency_prob.description: P(any month in (m, m+6] has delinquency status >= 1). Calibrated.

next_12m_default_prob.description: P(credit-event termination with zero-balance code in (02,03,09,15) OR delinquency status >= 6, within (m, m+12]). Calibrated.

next_12m_prepayment_prob.description: P(termination with zero-balance code 01 within (m, m+12]). Calibrated.

next_state.description: Predicted state at m+3. AUTHORED vocabulary; the document enumerates no state space. The delinquency tail 04-99 collapses into dq_90_plus because measured counts thin sharply beyond three months and per-state metrics on single-digit support would be noise presented as measurement.

exception_required.description: Whether the record requires reviewer exception handling. Integer 0/1 rather than a boolean literal so the CSV has one unambiguous rendering.

exception_type.description: Exception category. Values 2-6 derive from Section 6's description of validation_rules.json; values 7-8 from its description of servicer_updates.csv. MUST be exactly 'none' when exception_required is 0.

anomaly_score.description: Combined anomaly score. Higher is more anomalous. Normalised to [0,1] because the document states no scale; the normalisation rule is recorded in the model card.

top_drivers.description: Up to three semicolon-separated feature=signed_contribution pairs from the local attribution of the highest-probability outcome, ordered by descending absolute contribution. Semicolon rather than comma so the CSV needs no quoting. Signed, because 'this feature pushed risk down' is information a reviewer needs and an unsigned magnitude discards.

recommended_action.description: AUTHORED vocabulary; the document enumerates no action set. Produced by a deterministic decision table over model outputs and rule flags (anomaly/actions.py) — NEVER by generated text. This column is the one most at risk of a Principle I violation, so its owner is a decision table with no LLM dependency in its input closure.

confidence.description: Model-derived confidence in the row's headline prediction. The method is named per column in the model card; a bare number without its method is not reportable under Principle V.

x-file-level-assertions: Row count equals the number of scored loan-months in the score window recorded in artifacts/splits/split_definition.json.
No cell is null, empty, NaN, or infinite.
Column names and order match x-column-order exactly.
Rows are sorted ascending by (loan_id, reporting_month).
exception_required == 0 if and only if exception_type == 'none'.
Every reporting_month falls inside the score window.
